Method of Attack: Custom proxy-based phishing kit using reverse proxies to bypass multi-factor authentication by sitting in the middle between victim and email server, stealing authentication cookies to bypass MFA
Use of Beautiful Soup HTML and XML parsing tool to modify legitimate login pages and add phishing elements
Fingerprinting victims via JavaScript to reveal phishing page only to valid targets
Use of typo-squatted domains and password reset lure domains in phishing emails
Redirections via legitimate web resources and open redirects on platforms like Google Ads, Snapchat, DoubleClick
Hosting redirection code on web code editing/hosting services like CodeSandbox and Glitch
Impacted Systems: Corporate accounts in fin-tech, lending, accounting, insurance, and Federal Credit Union organizations in US, UK, New Zealand, Australia
Attack Vector: Phishing emails with embedded buttons or HTML attachments containing phishing URLs
Use of typo-squatted domains and password reset lure domains
Redirections through legitimate web resources and open redirects
Reverse proxy phishing kits intercepting login and MFA processes
Indicators of Compromise: Typo-squatted domains of legitimate Federal Credit Unions
Phishing domains: expiryrequest-mailaccess.com, expirationrequest-passwordreminder.com, emailaccess-passwordnotice.com, emailaccess-expirynotification.com
Redirection URLs hosted on Google Ads, Snapchat, DoubleClick, CodeSandbox, Glitch
Leaking phishing domain in server requests to Microsoft
